svg.text: Ordinary path-doubling by Boolean matrix multiplication
Illustrative dense all-pairs transitive-closure baseline: repeated squaring reveals longer and longer paths.
8 vertices, diagonal entries later set to 1 in the matrix.
teal dashed: appears in A^2 (up to 2-step paths)
orange dashed: appears in A^4 (up to 4-step paths)
A -> E and C -> G are not edges, but they appear after squaring.
B -> H needs three hops, so it first appears in A^4.
Rows and columns use the same vertex order A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H. Diagonal entries are 1.
Asymptotic takeaway for the dense-graph baseline
Processors: Theta(n^3) for standard Boolean matrix multiplication
Number of matrix multiplications: ceil(log_2 n) repeated squarings
Why the paper moves beyond it: strong NC depth, but very processor-heavy and tailored to dense all-pairs structure.
In this example, A^4 already reaches the closure because the longest relevant path has at most 4 edges.
